test_title: PYST 56: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which constitutional body is empowered to adjudicate legal disputes between the Centre and one or more states in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution, has the original jurisdiction to resolve disputes between:

 
 
• The Government of India and one or more states.
 
• The Government of India and any state(s) on one side and other states on the other.
 
• Two or more states.
 
 
 
• Such disputes must involve a question of law or fact on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends.
 
• Being the apex court, its decision is final and binding in such intergovernmental disputes.
 
• The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in such matters is exclusive and cannot be exercised by any other court in India.
 
• The Supreme Court also ensures the maintenance of the federal structure of India by acting as the ultimate arbiter in disputes between the Centre and the states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-State Council**:

 
 
• It is a non-constitutional body established under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution to promote coordination and cooperation between the Centre and states.
 
• The council is primarily advisory in nature, with the authority to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Centre and the states or among states.
 
• It plays a consultative role but does not have the power to adjudicate disputes.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission**:
 
 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an independent constitutional authority responsible for administering elections to the Parliament, state legislatures, and offices of the President and Vice-President.
 
• It ensures free and fair elections but does not have the authority to adjudicate disputes between the Centre and states.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission**:
 
 
• Established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is a constitutional body tasked with recommending the distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the states.
